headline: Phones cost more because AI wants the memory

sources.title: Google confirms Pixel 11 price increase due to RAM shortage
AI Data Centers Are Buying Up RAM and Raising Laptop Prices
The AI boom and the memory chip shortage

chunks.text: Google said on July 24 that its Pixel phones will cost more, and gave a reason people did not expect. The company is not paying more for design or for [[labor]]. It is paying more for [[memory]]. Memory is the set of [[chips]] that hold information while a phone is actually working, and it is separate from the [[storage]] where photos and apps sit. A senior Google [[manager]] said the company had {{held off}} on raising prices for as long as it could, but that the [[economics]] underneath had changed.

The numbers are [[steep]]. According to figures from one [[investment bank]], a [[gigabyte]] of this memory cost about 2.80 dollars in 2025 and costs about 12 dollars in 2026. That is [[roughly]] six times more in a single year. The Google manager said there had never been a rise in memory prices like the one the world is {{going through}} now. Reports suggest the next Pixel may {{cut back on}} memory compared with the [[model]] before it, with extra storage offered instead.

verbs.wrong: To buy from a different maker

chunks.text: The cause has nothing to do with phones. Companies building [[data centers]] for artificial intelligence have been {{buying up}} memory chips in enormous [[quantities]], and the factories cannot {{churn out}} enough to serve everyone. When a small number of very large buyers {{soak up}} the [[supply]], the price rises for everybody else. Phone makers, laptop makers and games [[console]] makers are all standing in the same line.

verbs.correct: To buy all that is for sale
verbs.wrong: To pay a higher price than others
To order something long in advance

chunks.text: This is why the story reaches people who have no interest in AI at all. Somebody replacing a broken phone in Manila or Lagos or Warsaw will {{pay out}} more this year, and the reason {{traces back}} to [[warehouses]] full of computers on another [[continent]]. Google announces its new phones on August 12. The rest of the [[industry]] is waiting to see whether [[rivals]] [[follow suit]] and {{put up}} their own prices, or {{hold out}} a little longer.
